draft.text:
{"letter":"Dear Hiring Manager,

Riverside Arena Group's calendar mixes concerts, sports and community events, and that mix is a big part of why this role caught my eye. For the past five years I've run social media and events for community sports organizations, and the job of getting people excited enough to show up is the part I enjoy most.

At Riverbend Youth Soccer League, I planned and ran a 40-team spring tournament that drew 600 attendees. I handled it from planning through the event itself, which taught me how much of a good event happens long before anyone arrives. Over two seasons there, I also grew our Instagram following from 2,400 to 9,100. A lot of that came from paying attention to what people actually responded to and doing more of it.

That same habit has shaped how I spend money. I cut our paid ad spend by 38% by shifting budget to player-made video, and I use Google Analytics to keep an eye on what's working. I know the stakes are different when you're tracking ticket sales across 60+ events a year, but I'd bring the same instinct to test, measure and adjust. Before Riverbend, I coordinated volunteer schedules for 25 community events a year at Harpeth Valley Rec Center, so I'm used to keeping a full calendar moving.

Writing has been a steady thread through all of it. At Harpeth Valley I wrote the weekly member newsletter for 3,000 subscribers, and my degree is in communication. Whether it's a newsletter, an Instagram caption or a campaign plan, I try to write the way people actually talk. I'm also looking forward to working alongside promoters and sponsors and learning how those partnerships shape an event's marketing from the start.

I'd love to talk about what's coming up on your calendar and how I could help fill the seats.

Thanks for your time,
Jordan Avery"}
